goal.objective:
In a fresh worktree /Users/FradSer/Developer/FradSer/git-agent/git-agent-intent on a new branch feat/staged-boundaries cut from develop, git-agent acts only on the split boundary the user has already expressed in the index, and reports when a file could be split, instead of inferring regions.

What must be true when this is met:

1. A run whose index already holds changes commits exactly the index content as its first commit, from the diff the index holds, without unstaging or re-staging anything. The defect reproduced on develop — a hand-staged region followed by `git commit --no-stage` puts unstaged work into the commit — does not happen. The unstaged remainder of the same file stays out of that commit.
2. `--no-stage` commits exactly what the index holds and nothing else, which is what its own help text already claims.
3. After that first commit, the remaining changes follow the existing file-level flow unchanged, so a run with an empty index behaves exactly as develop does.
4. When a changed file's own diff covers two or more git-anchored regions, the run reports that fact and names the regions and the command that splits them (`git add -p`), on the warning stream a scripted run also receives. No region is inferred, no content is rebuilt, and no index entry is written by git-agent itself.
5. No region policy remains: there is no gap, no size floor, no hunk inventory, no applier, no ledger, and nothing left to tune or measure. The production code this feature adds is a few hundred lines at most, and the model-free split measurement harness is not needed by it.
6. The working tree is never written to, and a preview (`--dry-run`) shows the same commits without committing.
7. Whole-file behavior for a run whose index is empty is byte-identical to develop: same prompts, same exit codes, same JSON fields, same commit content.

The branch carries a written comparison against feat/hunk-staging: production lines added, the behavior difference on the reproduced case, the risk each approach carries, and what the earlier measurement says about each.
goal.verificationContract:
- `cd /Users/FradSer/Developer/FradSer/git-agent/git-agent-intent && gofmt -l .` prints nothing; `make build` succeeds; `make test` passes with no FAIL line.
- A named e2e test reproduces the develop defect against the develop binary and shows the fix on this branch: with only the beta region staged by hand, the first commit carries the beta change and not the epsilon change, and the epsilon change is not silently absorbed.
- A named test proves `--no-stage` commits exactly the index content: the same fixture leaves the epsilon change uncommitted, and `git diff` (unstaged) still holds it.
- A named test proves a multi-region file produces the report naming its regions, and a single-region file produces none.
- A named test proves a run with an empty index on the same fixture commits the same content as develop (the two-binary differential: JSON envelope and commit subjects identical).
- `git diff develop feat/staged-boundaries --numstat` is reported, and the production-code total is compared with the 1447 lines feat/hunk-staging adds.
goal.completionClaim:
The four items the completion check named are now named tests, committed on branch feat/staged-boundaries in /Users/FradSer/Developer/FradSer/git-agent/git-agent-intent (527af48 "feat(app): commit the index as staged", c6aaf99 "test(e2e): compare this branch with develop"). Tree clean, develop and the hunk worktree untouched.

1. THE DEVELOP DEFECT AS A NAMED TEST, AGAINST THE DEVELOP BINARY
`TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_DevelopAbsorbsWhatTheBranchKeepsApart` builds the develop revision once from a detached worktree (removed afterwards, so the repository keeps no stale registration) and runs the same fixture through both binaries with only the func Beta region staged by hand. It prints `--- PASS` and logs:
  "develop: the staged commit absorbed the unstaged region, and the working tree was left empty"
and then asserts the branch does the opposite: HEAD holds `+ return "BETA"` and not `EPSILON`, and `git diff --name-only` still lists app.go. So the defect is reproduced against develop inside the suite, not in a shell script, and the same test shows the fix.
`TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_KeepsTheStagedRegionApart` (PASS) covers the full run: first commit = the staged region alone, second commit = the remainder alone, tree ends clean.

2. THE EMPTY-INDEX PARITY DIFFERENTIAL AS A NAMED TEST, WITH PROMPTS AND EXIT CODES
`TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_EmptyIndexMatchesDevelop` runs both binaries on identical fixtures with nothing staged, through a stub that records every request body. It asserts and logs:
  "empty index: 2 identical request(s), identical subjects, identical envelope, exit 0"
That is: equal exit codes, equal commit subjects, equal JSON envelopes after blanking SHAs, and request bodies byte-identical per request once the (differing) temp directory is stripped — so the prompts match, not just the commits.

3. THE DRY-RUN PREVIEW AS A NAMED TEST
`TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_DryRunPreviewsAndRestores` (PASS) asserts the envelope reports `dry_run: true` and the two commits a real run makes, that the first previewed commit is the staged content, that `git diff --cached` after the dry run equals the output before it byte for byte, that no commit is created, and that the real run then makes exactly the two previewed commits and leaves a clean tree.

4. `--no-stage` AND THE REPORT
`TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_NoStageCommitsTheIndexOnly` (PASS): one new commit holding only the staged region, the index empty afterwards, and `git diff` still holding the unstaged region. `TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_ReportsAMultiRegionFile` (PASS) asserts stderr carries "holds 2 separate regions" and "git add -p app.go" and that the run still commits one commit rather than splitting on its own; `TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_SingleRegionIsNotReported` (PASS) asserts a single-region change produces no such line.

SUITE AND SIZE
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing; `make build` succeeds; `make test` reports 18 packages ok and 0 FAIL lines. Production code added against develop: application/commit_service.go 100, application/staged_boundary.go 219, cmd/commit.go 3, infrastructure/git/client.go 26 = 348 lines, against 1447 on feat/hunk-staging, with no gap, floor, inventory, applier, ledger or content writer, so nothing is left to tune or measure.

WHAT THE APPROACH DOES
A run whose index holds changes commits exactly that content first, from the diff the index holds, without unstaging, restaging, rebuilding content, or writing an index entry. The remainder then follows develop's file-level flow. When a file the run is about to commit whole holds two or more git-anchored regions, it reports them and points at `git add -p`, on a stream cmd wires to stderr unconditionally so a scripted run reads it. The written comparison is at .memory/staged-boundaries-instead-of-inferred-regions.md.

FOUND AND FIXED ON THE WAY
The staged-content path first sent its diff to the model without the content filter or the byte cap; `TestCommitService_ByteCapAppliedBeforeGenerate` caught it, and the filter-and-cap tail of `prepareGroup` is now `preparedForModel`, shared by both paths. Six seam fixtures and two autonomous-root stubs were updated for the deliberate change (the staged content is its own commit; those stubs now plan the files the prompt listed).

LIMIT
The behaviour change reaches every run whose index holds changes, not only `--no-stage`: such a run now makes one more commit, because the staged content is its own commit rather than merged into the first group. That is the approach's point, it is stated in README and CHANGELOG, and it is why those fixtures changed.
